articles.title_original: Lululemon founder stuns Canadian women’s leadership conference with sexist comments
articles.title_zh: Lululemon founder stuns Canadian women’s leadership conference with sexist comments
facts_zh: Chip Wilson said men importing brides from Thailand was due to women waiting too long to have children The controversial founder of Lululemon suggested women in Canada are having too few children and this could lead some men to bring in brides from Thailand , in remarks that stunned audience members at a women’s leadership conference.

Chip Wilson, who built the Vancouver yoga-wear startup into a global athleisure empire, was a featured speaker at the Leadership Forum in Calgary earlier this week, an event organized by Axis Connects to advance women in leadership.
The organization says it aims to create space for “candid conversations about the barriers women face both in business and society”.

all_titles.en: Lululemon founder stuns Canadian women’s leadership conference with sexist comments

North Korea has ordered Switzerland's diplomatic representative to leave the country within 48 hours and called for the office to close amid a row over sanctions.
It said the move was in response to Switzerland's decision to place sanctions on the Songdowon international children's camp.
State media described this as "a blatant hostile act".

articles.title_zh: Colombian police storm supermarket to free 76 held hostage for 17 hours
facts_zh:
Colombian police storm supermarket to free 76 held hostage for 17 hours
- Published
Colombian security forces have freed around 76 shoppers and employees who had been held hostage for about 17 hours at a supermarket in the city of Cartagena.

Gunmen had stormed into the building at 08:00 local time (13:00 GMT) on Tuesday after what Colombian President Abelardo de la Espriella described as a failed attempt at robbing an armoured car carrying money.
They held those inside at gunpoint while trying to negotiate their getaway.

US stocks fall further as fears over AI intensify
- Published
Big technology firms connected to AI continued to see share prices fall on Wednesday, with stock in Nvidia and Anthropic dropping sharply in early trading.
The surge in Nvidia shares after boss Jensen Huang was reinstated was temporary, and the general stock sell-off continued, with all three main US stock market indices down.
The tech-dominated Nasdaq has shed over 2%.

articles.title_zh: US announces new tariffs on host of countries including China
facts_zh:
US announces new tariffs on host of countries including China
- Published
The US has announced a fresh raft of tariffs as President Donald Trump pushes ahead with his signature trade policy.
The new taxes charged on imports to America are set to hit many of the country's biggest trading partners - China, the European Union and 12 other jurisdictions.

The move follows the White House's investigation into the trade practices of other countries in March after the US Supreme Court ruled Trump's previously announced Liberation Day tariffs were illegal.

articles.title_original: Israeli strike kills senior Hamas security official and family in Gaza City
articles.title_zh: Israeli strike kills senior Hamas security official and family in Gaza City
facts_zh:
Israeli strike kills senior Hamas security official and family in Gaza City
- Published
An Israeli air strike in the Gaza Strip has killed a senior Hamas security official and three members of his family, according to local doctors and the Hamas-run interior ministry.

Mohammed Abu al-Ouf, 47, the head of Hamas's internal security service in northern Gaza, his wife and their two teenage daughters died when their apartment in Shati refugee camp in Gaza City was bombed at dawn, the ministry said.
The Israeli military said Abu al-Ouf was a "terrorist" and that he was eliminated "to remove the threat he posed".

all_titles.en: Israeli strike kills senior Hamas security official and family in Gaza City

articles.title_original: Huawei found guilty of stealing US trade secrets but acquitted of racketeering
articles.title_zh: Huawei found guilty of stealing US trade secrets but acquitted of racketeering
facts_zh:
Huawei found guilty of stealing US trade secrets but acquitted of racketeering
- Published
Huawei has been found guilty of conspiracy to steal trade secrets and bank fraud, but not guilty of the more serious overarching racketeering charge in a landmark case in the US.
In a two-month trial, prosecutors accused the Chinese technology and telecommunications giant of lying, cheating and stealing to gain any competitive advantage.
Huawei's defence team argued that prosecutors had decided Huawei was a criminal organisation and built its case from there, but the firm's success was due to its own innovation.

all_titles.en: Huawei found guilty of stealing US trade secrets but acquitted of racketeering

Protesters call on Israel to free Palestinian student held without charge
- Published
Israeli students, activists and academics are calling for the release of a Palestinian undergraduate who was taken from his university dormitory by Israeli police earlier this month and has since been held without charge.
Mahdi Tunsi, a 26-year-old sociology and criminology student at the Hebrew University of Jerusalem, appeared in an Israeli court in the city on Tuesday - a hearing that was held behind closed doors.
Israeli police say he was arrested "concerning ties to an act of terrorism".
